diana (customer): Hey @support - after the control plane IP rotation yesterday our Private control plane endpoint in us-west is seeing immediate TLS failures from our app fleet. Clients report "TLS handshake failed" and we see lots of TCP RSTs right after ClientHello.

sarah (support): can you share a small tcpdump and confirm which control plane host you're targeting?

diana (customer): target is cp-usw1.private.redwood.example.com. tcpdump snippet (ports redacted):

```
08:12:44.123456 IP 10.0.4.22.54321 > 54.234.12.34.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 12345 ecr 0,nop,wscale 7], length 0
08:12:44.123457 IP 54.234.12.34.443 > 10.0.4.22.54321: Flags [S.], seq 100, ack 1, win 28960, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 67890 ecr 12345], length 0
08:12:44.123458 IP 10.0.4.22.54321 > 54.234.12.34.443: Flags [.], ack 101, win 65280, length 0
08:12:44.123459 IP 10.0.4.22.54321 > 54.234.12.34.443: Flags [P.], seq 1:512, ack 101, win 65280, length 511
    <ClientHello TLSv1.2, length 507>
08:12:44.123460 IP 54.234.12.34.443 > 10.0.4.22.54321: Flags [R], seq 0, win 0, length 0
```

diana (customer): immediate RST from the server side after ClientHello.

devon (eng): pattern S -> S. -> ClientHello -> RST commonly points to either an inline device rejecting the handshake (TLS proxy, firewall) or a server-side accept path dropping sockets because of NAT/asymmetric routing. Two quick checks: 1) do you run a stateful NAT with aggressive conntrack timeouts? 2) any TLS inspection that might rewrite SNI?

mike (ops): also ensure your network allows ephemeral ports so the client NAT mapping can accept return flow from the server. If the provider rewrites source ports, short conntrack lifetimes can kill in-flight handshakes.

diana (customer): we do use a managed NAT that rotates ephemeral ports and vendor docs show an ESTABLISHED timeout of 30s. How can we prove conntrack is the culprit?

devon (eng): reproduce with openssl s_client -msg + tcpdump at the same time. If you see ClientHello and then a RST with no ServerHello, it strongly implicates the return path or a middlebox. Commands: 

```
# on an app host
openssl s_client -connect 54.234.12.34:443 -servername cp-usw1.private.redwood.example.com -msg
sudo tcpdump -nni eth0 host 54.234.12.34 and port 443 -w /tmp/cp-debug.pcap
```

devon (eng): also check for asymmetric routing where return packets egress a different NAT and lose the conntrack entry.

diana (customer): ran the suggested test. openssl shows ClientHello then immediate RST. snippet: 

```
>>> ClientHello
<<< RST
139736...:error:140770FC:SSL routines:SSL23_GET_SERVER_HELLO:unknown protocol:ssl/record/ssl_lib.c:... 
```

sarah (support): quick operational checks: 1) did you update perimeter allowlists with the new control-plane IPs we published during the rotation? 2) any load-balancer or edge device that could be rewriting source IPs?

diana (customer): we updated DNS entries but missed adding the rotated control-plane IPs to our firewall allowlist. Firewall policy only permits flows to known IPs and drops unrouted new connections.

mike (ops): that matches the trace. When the control-plane IPs aren't allowed, the firewall or NAT may not accept the initial flow properly and can trigger an RST from our edge when it can't allocate state. Mitigation steps: add the new control-plane CIDR to your allowlist, and increase conntrack timeout on the NAT.

devon (eng): recommended immediate mitigations:
- Add new edge CIDR (example: 54.234.12.0/24) to your egress/ingress allowlist for control-plane comms
- Increase nf_conntrack tcp established timeout to >= 300s (avoid 30s vendor default)
- If you run an inline TLS inspector, bypass cp-usw1.* while you update rules

devon (eng): debugging commands if it reoccurs:
```
sudo conntrack -L | grep 54.234.12.34
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=300
```

infra-bot: control-plane IP rotation completed for us-west at 2025-11-02T03:10:00Z. Published new edge CIDRs to partner portal.

diana (customer): I added the CIDR, bumped conntrack timeout to 600s, and bypassed the TLS inspector for the control plane hostname. After changes, openssl now completes and our app telemetry shows TLS sessions established. Verified tcpdump: 

```
08:45:12.555 IP 10.0.4.22.54321 > 54.234.12.34.443: Flags [S]
08:45:12.555 IP 54.234.12.34.443 > 10.0.4.22.54321: Flags [S.]
08:45:12.555 IP 10.0.4.22.54321 > 54.234.12.34.443: Flags [.], ack
08:45:12.556 TLS  -> ServerHello ...
```

sarah (support): great — we'll add a KB article: "Private: update firewall allowlists and conntrack settings after control-plane IP rotations". Also asking eng about an advisory webhook for rotations.

devon (eng): follow-up idea: expose a small rotation preflight that initiates short-lived connections from our edge to keep customer NAT mappings warm during rotations (reduces impact for customers with strict per-IP rules).

diana (customer): thanks everyone — that fixed it :tada:
